title: Plasma Immersion Ion Implantation of AISI 316L Stainless Steel Parts Manufactured by Laser Powder Bed Fusion
container-title: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Austenitic stainless steel (SS) AISI 316L is highly compatible with laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), an advanced additive manufacturing (AM) technique for producing high-quality near-net-shape parts with complex geometries, especially for aerospace and medical applications. To further enhance its surface properties, temperature-controlled nitrogen plasma immersion ion implantation (TC-NPIII) was applied to LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L to obtain an expanded austenite (
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N) layer, thereby enhancing surface performance and expanding the applicability of this material in demanding environments. The present work investigates the influence of TC-NPIII treatment temperature and duration on the microstructural evolution and mechanical performance of LPBF-manufactured AISI 316L. Samples were produced by LPBF in a laser-adapted powder bed system and subsequently treated by TC-NPIII, varying treatment duration for 1 and 3 h at controlled temperatures (450-520 °C). Microstructural analysis after treatment revealed a modified layer with a thickness that ranged from approximately 18.30 to 28.40 µm, superimposed on the characteristic LPBF microstructure. Grazing Incidence x-ray Diffraction (GI-XRD) analysis confirmed the formation of the desired
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N phase, while no diffraction peaks associated with chromium nitrides were detected within the investigated processing window. Cross-sectional nanoindentation measurements of the treated samples yielded hardness values of approximately 386-751 HV, representing a substantial increase compared with the untreated LPBF sample (238 HV). These results indicate that, among the treatment temperatures and durations investigated, 450 °C for 3 h represents the optimal processing condition, promoting
                    <jats:italic>γ</jats:italic>
                    N formation while preventing chromium nitride precipitation. The present work demonstrates that TC-NPIII can effectively produce expanded austenite and achieve significant surface hardening within treatment durations as short as 1-3 h. Moreover, these findings confirm the effectiveness of the TC-NPIII treatment in modifying the surface of LPBF-produced AISI 316L stainless steel, thereby enhancing its mechanical performance while preserving the characteristic hierarchical microstructure generated during LPBF.
                  </jats:p>

title: Lightweight YOLOv8n Improvement for Steel Surface Defect Detection and TensorRT Inference Acceleration

affiliation.name: School of Dundee International Institute, Central South University

abstract: <jats:p>Steel surface defect detection demands both reliable accuracy and real-time inference performance for practical industrial deployment. This paper investigates a lightweight improvement of YOLOv8n by replacing selected backbone downsampling convolution layers with GhostConv modules. To evaluate the effect of replacement depth, three variants (Ghost-1, Ghost-2, Ghost-4) are compared with the baseline under the same training protocol. The NEU-DET dataset is re-split with a stratified 8:1:1 ratio into 1441 training, 180 validation, and 179 test images. Experimental results show that Ghost-2, which replaces layers 5 and 7, achieves the best mAP@0.5 of 0.832, exceeding baseline by 0.008. However, the baseline remains superior on the stricter mAP@0.5:0.95 metric (0.495 vs. 0.475 for Ghost-2). TensorRT FP16 deployment provides approximately 2× speedup for both models: baseline latency reduces from 10.64 ms to 5.32 ms, while Ghost-2 reduces from 12.21 ms to 5.55 ms. Ghost-2 retains a slight mAP@0.5 advantage on TensorRT FP16 but is 4.3% slower. The results indicate that partial GhostConv replacement can improve coarse detection accuracy, yet strict localization accuracy and deployment latency require careful trade-off.</jats:p>

title: Cold Atmospheric Plasma on Dental Implants: One Reactive‐Species Mechanism and the Dose That Protocols Do Not Report

affiliation.name: Department of Dentistry, College of Medicine Yeungnam University Daegu South Korea
Department of Dentistry and Prosthodontics Daegu Catholic University School of Medicine Daegu South Korea

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Cold atmospheric plasma is applied to dental implants for surface activation, osseointegration, infection control and host modulation. This review reads those four uses as one reactive‐species mechanism with a separate exposure axis per target (an organizing interpretation, not a measured law) and audits what an illustrative sample of thirty‐three protocols reports about dose. Plasma medicine has a source‐characterization specification (DIN SPEC 91315) and candidate dose descriptors, delivered energy and equivalent total oxidation potential, whose inputs no audited protocol reports in full. Of twenty‐five atmospheric‐pressure protocols, working gas is stated in twenty‐four, flow in nineteen, power or voltage setting in eleven; across all thirty‐three, treated area and delivered dose in none, a measured output in two. Human endpoints are mostly surrogates.</jats:p>

title: Modelling space weather plasma physics

affiliation.name: KU Leuven, Celestijnenlaan 200B
Institute of Physics, University of Maria Curie-Skłodowska

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We start with a brief introduction to the many faces of the Sun, the dynamic star that is the main source of space weather. We explain the need for spacecraft observations, the structure of the solar atmosphere, and the Sun’s magnetic cycle. Next, we focus on the Sun’s influence on Earth, define ‘space weather,’ and briefly discuss its effects on our technology and related socio-economic impacts. Then, we present data-driven, physics-based simulation models with predictive capabilities that enable forecasting and mitigation. We focus on models developed by my team at KU Leuven and the results and predictions they produce: the heliospheric wind and CME evolution models EUHFORIA and ICARUS, the global solar corona model COCONUT, and the solar energetic particle acceleration and transport model Particle Radiation Asset Directed at IP Space Exploration. We end with a few take-home messages.</jats:p>

title: Structural thresholds and nonlinear acceleration in clinical trial failure: a generalised additive model and change-point analysis of 134,724 registered trials (2016–2025)
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Prior analyses of clinical trial termination have primarily modelled protocol complexity as a linear predictor of termination risk. However, linear models cannot detect structural inflection points, defined as values beyond which marginal increases in protocol complexity produce disproportionate acceleration in termination probability. Identifying these inflection points would transform protocol complexity from a continuous risk factor into a concrete planning threshold for protocol design.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Using a population-based cohort of 134,724 interventional trials from ClinicalTrials.gov (2016–2025), we modelled the relationship between protocol design features and trial termination using generalised additive models (GAMs) with penalised regression splines. Structural change-points were evaluated using the PELT algorithm with 1000 bootstrap resamples and temporal validation (training cohort: 2016–2021; validation cohort: 2022–2025). Reviewer-requested supplementary analyses included multivariable logistic regression adjusting for trial phase, sponsor class, intervention characteristics, geographical scope, allocation, masking, and outcome burden; formal interaction modelling; model diagnostic assessment; follow-up maturity sensitivity analyses; entropy robustness analyses; and counterfactual scenario modelling.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      GAM smoothing functions confirmed highly non-linear relationships for eligibility criteria (edf = 17.15,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001), total endpoints (edf = 16.96,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001), and the Protocol-Burden Index (edf = 17.14,
                      <jats:italic>P</jats:italic>
                       < 0.001). Bootstrap-supported change-point analysis identified an eligibility threshold at 16 criteria (95% CI 16–21), while temporal validation identified a corresponding threshold at 21 criteria. Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that protocol complexity remained independently associated with trial termination after adjustment for major trial characteristics. Formal interaction analyses demonstrated significant effect modification by both trial phase and sponsor class. Model diagnostics demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC = 0.716) and good numerical stability. Entropy sensitivity analyses consistently showed higher termination rates among protocols with increasingly concentrated structural burden. Under an equal-susceptibility counterfactual scenario, redesign of above-threshold protocols to below-threshold complexity corresponded to an estimated reduction of 5560 observed terminations (26.2% of terminated trials) under the specified counterfactual scenario.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Clinical trial termination risk exhibits robust nonlinear associations with protocol complexity across multiple complementary analytical approaches. The identified eligibility threshold should be interpreted as a population-level planning benchmark rather than a deterministic cutoff. These findings support prospective evaluation of complexity-aware trial design strategies and provide quantitative benchmarks for future protocol optimisation.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Luminescent Molecular Logic: Fundamentals, Implementation Strategies, and Emerging Architectures

affiliation.name: Departamento de Física and IUdEA Universidad de La Laguna  San Cristóbal de La Laguna Santa Cruz de Tenerife Spain

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The increasing demand for energy‐efficient, adaptable, and environment‐responsive information processing is motivating the exploration of computing paradigms that complement conventional silicon electronics. Among these, luminescent molecular logic offers a versatile approach in which chemical, physical, or optical stimuli are converted into measurable photophysical outputs and interpreted according to Boolean operations. This Review critically examines the principles, implementation, and validation of luminescent molecular logic, with particular emphasis on the methodological transition from continuous optical signals to reproducible digital outputs. A systematic framework is discussed encompassing photophysical measurements, response‐function selection, uncertainty propagation, signal digitization, threshold definition, truth‐table construction, and logic‐gate assignment. Particular attention is also given to the distinction between independent optical channels and mathematically derived response functions, as well as to interrogation‐level reconfiguration, data‐analysis‐level reassignment, and material‐level reprogramming. Quantitative figures of merit are introduced to assess state discrimination, reproducibility, stability, crosstalk, and scalability beyond qualitative gate assignment. Representative supramolecular, photochromic, DNA‐based, carbon‐dot, and trivalent‐lanthanide platforms are critically compared in terms of their capabilities, limitations, and prospects for integration. Finally, current bottlenecks and emerging opportunities in multidimensional luminescence, adaptive architectures, and hybrid molecular–photonic and molecular–electronic systems are discussed.</jats:p>

title: From Static Structural Coloration to Dynamic Photonics in Metal–Organic and Covalent–Organic Frameworks

affiliation.name: Department of Functional Materials and Catalysis University of Vienna  Vienna Austria

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent–organic frameworks (COFs) combine structural tunability, accessible porosity, and chemically responsive interiors, making them attractive photonic building blocks. Yet in framework‐dominated static architectures, porosity can reduce dielectric contrast and increase the structural coherence required for strong macroscopic optical responses, while disorder, scattering, and processing‐induced defects can further weaken color saturation. This Review examines how refractive‐index contrast, optical interaction depth, positional correlation, scattering, and mechanical integrity collectively govern static MOF‐ and COF‐based photonic platforms. It then discusses dynamic strategies in which pore occupancy, framework dimensions, particle organization, and competing optical pathways become externally addressable through chemical, thermal, mechanical, electric, or magnetic stimuli. Rather than treating porosity and disorder solely as limitations, this Review highlights their potential as functional degrees of freedom. A central design principle therefore emerges, in which photonic performance should be optimized by controlling the type and length scale of order required for a targeted optical function.</jats:p>

title: Non‐Hermitian Induced Unidirectional Guided Resonance

affiliation.name: Key laboratory of Quantum Materials and Devices of Ministry of Education School of Physics Southeast University Nanjing China
Key laboratory of Quantum Materials and Devices of Ministry of Education School of Physics Southeast University Nanjing China

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We propose a method to realize unidirectional guided resonance (UGR) by modulating non‐Hermitian parameters. Owing to the flexible tunability of these parameters, we further merge an exceptional point (EP) with a UGR to form an EP‐UGR point. Our scheme is based on a three‐band system analytically described by a tight‐binding model and implemented in a photonic crystal. Introducing gain and loss induces the UGR: parameter variations split a bound state in the continuum (BIC) into two ‐points. Because the ‐points associated with upward radiation and downward radiation evolve differently, only the downward radiation ‐points re‐merge as the non‐Hermitian parameter varies, thereby forming the UGR. Introducing an additional asymmetry parameter produces an EP. Temporal coupled‐mode theory predicts the existence of the EP‐UGR point, which is realized by precise multi‐parameter tuning that merges the UGR and EP. This work deepens the understanding of UGR formation and provides new insights into light–matter interactions, laser design, and on‐chip photonic devices.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>O envelhecimento cutâneo é um processo biológico multifatorial caracterizado pela degradação da integridade estrutural e da matriz extracelular (MEC). Para mitigar essas alterações morfológicas, a medicina regenerativa tem impulsionado terapias minimamente invasivas baseadas em hemoderivados. Este estudo tem como objetivo avaliar e comparar a eficácia clínica, a segurança e os mecanismos de ação tecidual das terapias autólogas de primeira e segunda geração, destacando a indispensabilidade da atuação técnica do biomédico na padronização pré-analítica. Trata-se de uma Revisão Integrativa da Literatura conduzida nas bases de dados PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science e BVS/LILACS. Após o rigoroso delineamento de elegibilidade, 15 artigos científicos (publicados entre 2020 e 2026) compuseram a amostra final. Os achados demonstram que, enquanto os concentrados de primeira geração apresentam uma liberação rápida de fatores de crescimento (bolus), a segunda geração forma uma rede tridimensional fisiológica, garantindo uma eluição sustentada e o aprisionamento funcional de leucócitos. Clinicamente, ambas as terapias induzem expressiva neocolagenogênese e aumento da espessura dérmica. Topograficamente, a segunda geração demonstra superioridade no preenchimento estrutural periorbital (textura e crepitação), enquanto a primeira se destaca no clareamento de hiperpigmentações infraorbitais. A acentuada heterogeneidade nos protocolos de centrifugação figura como o principal gargalo metodológico da literatura atual. Conclui-se que essas matrizes constituem estratégias altamente eficazes, contudo, o domínio sobre a fisiologia do processamento e a padronização operacional (força g e tempo) pelo biomédico são determinantes para a reprodutibilidade clínica e a segurança do paciente.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Precise modulation of carrier dynamics in two‐dimensional (2D) materials is pivotal for the advancement of ultrafast optoelectronics and terahertz (THz) technologies. THz spectroscopy, with its ability to probe photoconductivity on ultrashort timescales without contact effects, serves as a typical tool for this purpose. With particular emphasis on terahertz time‐domain spectroscopy (THz‐TDS) and optical pump–THz probe (OPTP) spectroscopy, this article reviews carrier transport and ultrafast dynamics in representative 2D material systems, including graphene, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), MXenes, and other material classes with extensive THz studies. Special attention is devoted to the regulation of carrier dynamics, interfacial charge‐transfer mechanisms in heterostructures, and their correlations with device performance. Rather than attempting an exhaustive survey of all 2D material families or all THz spectroscopic methodologies, this review adopts a focused perspective on how THz spectroscopy can connect microscopic carrier processes with tunable optoelectronic properties and device functionalities. By synthesizing these insights, this review aims to provide a focused framework for understanding and exploiting the THz optoelectronic properties of 2D materials.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This review surveys the development of uncooled and thermoelectrically cooled photon‐counting detectors capable of single‐photon detection. It introduces photon‐counting principles and key performance metrics, including quantum efficiency (QE), photon detection efficiency (PDE), dark count rate (DCR), afterpulsing, dead time, timing jitter, spectral range, and fill factor. Major detector classes include photomultiplier tubes (PMTs), microchannel plate photomultipliers (MCP‐PMTs), hybrid photon detectors (HPDs), single‐photon avalanche diodes (SPADs), silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs), III–V and germanium‐on‐silicon (Ge‐on‐Si) SPADs, and CMOS‐integrated SPAD arrays. Charge‐integration technologies, including EMCCDs, sCMOS/qCMOS sensors, and quanta image sensors (QIS), are also considered in the context of single‐photon sensitivity. The review examines trade‐offs between sensitivity, timing resolution, noise, spectral coverage, scalability, and system integration. Tolerance to excessive optical power is discussed for field‐deployed quantum communication and LiDAR systems. Emerging low‐dimensional and novel semiconductor detectors are critically assessed, distinguishing Geiger‐mode operation from alternative high‐gain approaches. Frequency‐upconversion detection is considered as a complementary approach to room‐temperature photon counting beyond the near‐infrared. Finally, representative detector systems are compared in terms of spectral range, PDE/QE, timing jitter, DCR, operating temperature, and applications.</jats:p>

title: A simple model for evaporation-driven migration of liquid metal between plasma pulses in a fusion reactor with liquid metal plasma-facing components

affiliation.name: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Liquid metal plasma-facing components (PFCs) are being considered for a variety of fusion power plant designs, and careful control of the liquid metal inventory will be essential in these systems to mitigate challenges with liquid metal corrosion and hydrogen fuel retention. Since many power plant designs and existing test facilities rely on pulsed plasma sources, it is critical to understand how liquid metal evaporation leads to material migration within a reactor over the periods of time when no plasma is present. This work addresses this question by developing a simple particle balance model to efficiently calculate liquid metal vapor transport patterns over indefinitely long time periods, using a particle redistribution matrix to capture the vapor transport details. After developing the mathematical model, characteristics of a future Liquid Metal Core-Edge (LMCE) research facility with liquid lithium divertors are used as a reference to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used. Examples of lithium migration during the cooldown period between plasma pulses show that the pattern of lithium deposition depends primarily on the system geometry. An important secondary effect in these scenarios is the relative cooldown rate of the lithium divertor with respect to other PFCs in the device. Examples are also provided to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used to optimize the design of a cold finger to collect liquid metal condensation for extraction and reprocessing, with the results showing that a future LMCE facility may be capable of collecting all of the lithium evaporated between plasma pulses if the main chamber walls can be maintained above 350 C during operation.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Optical neural networks (ONNs), particularly diffractive neural networks (DNNs), offer a promising computational paradigm owing to their high speed, intrinsic parallelism, and low energy consumption. However, most demonstrated DNNs are static, with their functionalities fixed after fabrication. Although several reconfigurable architectures such as spatial light modulators (SLMs) and electrically controlled digital‐coding metasurfaces have been demonstrated, they often suffer from high power consumption and limited scalability. Here, we introduce an electrochemically reconfigurable diffractive neural network (ECDNN) based on a PANI‐functionalized Pancharatnam‐Berry (PB) phase metasurface, whose optical response is reversibly controlled through electrochemical redox reactions. Using a simultaneous multi‐objective optimization (SMOO) strategy, different computational tasks can be mapped to distinct state configurations. As a proof of concept, we demonstrate a single‐layer ECDNN capable of performing two classification tasks. The system exhibits response times of 30–40 ms for optical transmission under sub‐volt driving voltages, enabling low‐power operation and facilitating compatibility with low‐voltage driving electronics. Numerical studies further extend the state‐conditioned framework to a two‐layer architecture with four predefined state combinations. This work provides a fast, energy‐efficient, and high‐neuron‐density hardware platform for brain‐inspired optical computing.</jats:p>

title:

Yet Nonexclusive Role

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Separating thermal and laser intensity effects in plasmonic photocatalysis has proven challenging because the two are frequently intertwined. Higher laser intensities will increase any laser-induced heating, making it difficult to isolate the influence of laser intensity and complicating efforts to disentangle thermal versus nonthermal contributions to plasmonic photocatalysis. Here, we decouple laser intensity and laser heating effects by fabricating plasmonic nanostructures with nearly identical optical properties but divergent thermal properties, allowing us to modulate and even eliminate laser heating while applying the same range of laser intensities. We simultaneously perform upconverting nanoparticle (UCNP)-based microscale thermometry and monitor the photocatalyzed dimerization of 4-nitrothiophenol (4-NTP) to 4,4′-dimercaptoazobenzene (DMAB) with Raman spectroscopy. We show that larger temperature rises enhance the reaction and, even more importantly, the temperature rise alone dictates the degree of 4-NTP to DMAB conversion, independent of the applied laser intensity. These results are consistent across two different plasmonic nanostructures. External heating combined with a threshold laser intensity can also drive the reaction, with the degree of conversion again determined solely by the temperature rise. However, despite the critical influence of the temperature rise, external heating alone fails to catalyze the reaction. Leveraging ultrahigh thermal conductivity diamond substrates, which let us increase the laser intensity without inducing heating, we further demonstrate that higher laser intensities increase the reaction rate yet have no effect on the degree of conversion. Thus, although temperature plays an outsize role, the plasmonic photocatalysis process nonetheless cannot be explained by a purely thermal mechanism.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The unresolved complex mixture (UCM) consists of chromatographically unresolvable branched, cyclic, and aromatic hydrocarbons, which are intermediate- to semivolatile organic compounds primarily derived from anthropogenic fossil fuel usage, including industrial emissions and gasoline and diesel exhaust. The UCM in natural archives, expressed as its ratio to resolved compounds (UCM/R), may thus provide an indication of fossil fuel-derived contamination in the environment over time. To test this hypothesis, accurately dated sediment records from the Black Sea, the Baltic Sea, and the northeastern Germany Tiefer See lake were analyzed for hydrocarbons. Each record presents a similar temporal pattern with a synchronous main increase of UCM/R in the early 1950s and a decrease in the 1990s. This UCM/R pattern most likely reflects the pronounced increase in the use of petroleum-derived products during the Great Acceleration of the mid-20th century and, subsequently, the application of filters and catalytic converters to reduce volatile organic compound emissions in the 1980s–1990s. Therefore, UCM/R in recent sediments represents a stratigraphic anthropogenic marker for the Great Acceleration in European midlatitudes and, if replicated globally, could be a further marker for the beginning of the Anthropocene as a potential geological epoch.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Point Cloud Neural Network (PCNN) plays an essential role in various 3D applications, with some of them even being time-sensitive and safety-critical. However, the large scale of unordered points with lengthy features results in heavy computational workloads, making them far from real-time processing. To address this challenge, we propose PQuant, a Morton-code-based fine-grained quantization for accelerating both point-based and voxel-based networks. Specifically, we utilize Morton-code to capture the inherent point similarity and the voxel distribution. Considering the similarity among near points’ features, we decompose features into base and offsets, where the offsets typically exhibit a narrow dynamic range and can thus be quantized using low precision. For the voxel-based networks, spatial location indicated by Morton-codes allows PQuant to apply high precision representation to distant voxels, which are generally sparser and more sensitive to quantization. From the hardware aspect, PQuant integrates a reconfigurable mixed-precision systolic array designed to handle both dense and sparse mixed-precision convolutions in PCNNs. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PQuant achieves 3.7 × and 3.5 × speedup and 5.2 × and 6.0 × energy savings over state-of-the-art PCNN accelerator PointAcc for the point-based and voxel-based networks, respectively.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Based on the energy confinement time scaling law of stellarator in the low-confinement mode, combined with energy balance equation and the plasma propagation and power deposition equations of the electron cyclotron wave in the three-dimensional magnetic field, a stellarator plasma start-up model including electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) and impurity radiation power loss is established. Validation against W7-X experimental data demonstrates good agreement in the temporal evolution of electron temperature and radiation losses, which verified that the model can correctly give the plasma start-up results of the stellarator under ECRH. This model is applied to predict the results of plasma start-up under 28 GHz ECRH for China Helical Device 1 (CN-H1) stellarator. The effects of the initial electron-to-ion temperature ratio (Te/Ti), ECRH injection power (Pinj), deposition position and effective charge number Z_{\text{eff}} on start-up are systematically studied and analyzed. The results show that the initial Te/Ti ratio affects only the ramp-up rate, while the final steady-state electron and ion temperature remain unaffected. Higher Pinj accelerates electron temperature rise and increases flat-top electron temperature, whereas the ion temperature exhibits the opposite trend, decreasing with increasing Pinj. The deposition location has a decisive impact on the start-up outcome: only core deposition on the low-field side leads to a successful start-up, while high-field side and off-axis low-field side depositions fail owing to refractive deviation of the ray trajectory and insufficient absorption, respectively. The steady-state electron and ion temperatures are insensitive to {\mathrm{Z}}_{\text{eff}} within a reasonable range.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a rapidly growing neurological disorder characterized by motor and non-motor symptoms associated with mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress. Photobiomodulation (PBM) may modulate mitochondrial pathways. This randomized, controlled, single-blind pilot trial investigated intranasal and transpalatal PBM, individually or combined, in 48 individuals with idiopathic PD allocated to TP + IN (intranasal + transpalatal PBM), IN (intranasal PBM), TP (transpalatal PBM), or Sham. Participants underwent 24 sessions over 12 weeks using near-infrared light (808 nm, 100 mW, 60 J, or 120 J per point). Outcomes were assessed at baseline (T1), 1 week after the intervention (T2), and 1-month follow-up (T3) using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and Movement Disorder Society-Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS). Forty participants completed the study. IN significantly improved MoCA and MDS-UPDRS scores, with benefits persisting at follow-up. Sham showed a decline in MoCA. These findings suggest that intranasal PBM may be a promising adjunctive therapy for PD; further studies are needed to elucidate mechanisms and optimize treatment protocols.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Hollow‐core anti‐resonant fibers (HC‐ARFs) have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional solid‐core fibers (SCFs) by combining low loss, broad transmission bandwidth, ultra‐low nonlinearity, low dispersion, and reduced latency. This review critically examines advances in HC‐ARFs from structural evolution and guiding physics to applications and deployment. We trace the progression from Kagome and single‐ring designs to nested and double‐nested architectures, and discuss anti‐resonant reflection, inhibited coupling, cladding density of photonic states, major loss mechanisms, and machine‐learning‐assisted prediction and design. We further review applications in ultrafast and nonlinear optics, gas and mid‐infrared lasers, ultraviolet guidance, high‐power delivery and extreme photonics, as well as high‐capacity, ultra‐wideband, long‐haul, quantum, and advanced optical communications. Particular attention is given to fabrication tolerances, reproducibility, bending sensitivity, interconnection, environmental stability, scalability, cost, and system‐level integration. Finally, we identify remaining bottlenecks and prospects for beyond‐fifth‐generation and sixth‐generation networks, artificial‐intelligence data interconnection, next‐generation optical networks, quantum technologies, high‐power laser delivery, and extreme photonics.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The Stokes parameters are three real parameters that completely characterize partially coherent light spanned by two modes – whether a pair of polarization or spatial modes – whose use is ubiquitous in optics. Whereas the Stokes parameters are defined through an expansion of the  coherence matrix in terms of Pauli matrices, it has been theorized that the  Gell–Mann matrices – developed in high‐energy particle physics – can serve as a basis for  coherence matrices for three‐mode light. This entails eight Stokes–Gell–Mann (SGM) parameters required for the polarization of non‐paraxial fields (spanned by three polarization modes), and fields comprising three spatial or temporal modes. Here we present the first measurements of the SGM parameters for partially coherent three‐mode light in a photonic integrated platform comprising a hexagonal mesh of Mach–Zehnder interferometers. Measuring the SGM parameters on chip, from which we reconstruct the  coherence matrix, facilitates exploring the full space of iso‐entropy fields that can be inter‐converted into each other unitarily and those that cannot. These results pave the way to utilizing multimode partially coherent light in applications involving optical communications, sensing, and information processing.</jats:p>

<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Polarization control is essential for modern optical systems. Recently, 2D materials featuring highly anisotropic absorption across broad wavelength regions have emerged as a promising solution for realizing optical polarizers with operation bandwidths far exceeding those achievable using bulk materials. Despite this, existing 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers face critical limitations in simultaneously delivering high polarizer figures of merit (FOMs), robust power endurance, and scalable fabrication, hindering their practical deployment beyond the laboratory. Here, we overcome this bottleneck by demonstrating optical polarizers through integrating 2D MXene films onto silicon photonic devices and subsequently converting them in situ into 2D titanium dioxide (TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    ). The 2D TiO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    exhibits significantly improved anisotropic absorption and thermal/chemical stability compared with MXene, enabling the hybrid polarizers that achieve high polarizer FOMs of up to ∼19.3 (a record among 2D‐material‐coated devices) and excellent power tolerance (stable under > 2 W coupled average power), together with a broad operation bandwidth (> 140 nm) and a high fabrication yield (∼98%). We also demonstrate microring resonator polarizers achieving high polarization extinction ratios of up to ∼12 dB. With outstanding overall performance and strong potential for large‐scale manufacturing, these devices represent a solid step toward industrial implementation of 2D‐material‐based optical polarizers.
                  </jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Periodically driven coupled waveguides provide an ideal platform for exploring nonlinear Floquet dynamics. While nonlinear states matching the driving period are well‐understood, multi‐period Floquet states—which break discrete time‐translation symmetry and are closely related to discrete time crystals—remain largely unexplored, especially beyond the period‐doubling regime and in their connection to T‐periodic states. Here, we reveal multi‐period nonlinear states that bifurcate from their T‐periodic counterparts in a waveguide‐based Floquet system. By utilizing the phase angle of the Floquet multiplier governing T‐periodic state stability, we establish a general rule to identify the bifurcation point. In the weak nonlinearity regime, stable and unstable branches of multi‐period nonlinear states bifurcate precisely at this point, whereas a slight shift occurs under strong nonlinearity. Using this framework, we discover multi‐period Floquet states beyond the period‐doubling regime. Our work uncovers a fundamental link between T‐periodic and multi‐period nonlinear solutions, opening new avenues for designing discrete‐time‐crystal‐inspired photonic devices.</jats:p>

Efficacy of low-level laser therapy in scar treatment: an integrative review
abstract: <jats:p>Scar formation is a physiological tissue repair process that may lead to structural and functional changes affecting tissue mobility, elasticity, and overall tissue quality. In this context, low-level laser therapy has been investigated as a complementary physiotherapeutic approach for scar management. This study aimed to analyze the effects of low-level laser therapy in the treatment of scars, considering its potential benefits for tissue repair and scar characteristics. This literature review was conducted through the analysis of scientific studies addressing the use of laser therapy and photobiomodulation in different types of scars. A total of 16 articles were selected, eight of which were considered more closely related to the research objective and were included in the discussion. The analyzed studies reported favorable outcomes regarding scar thickness, elasticity, pigmentation, pliability, pain, and pruritus, although differences were observed according to scar type, therapeutic modality, treatment parameters, and intervals between sessions. It was concluded that low-level laser therapy has potential as a complementary resource in physiotherapeutic scar management, requiring individualized treatment and continuous assessment of clinical response. Further studies with greater methodological standardization are needed to establish more consistent therapeutic parameters.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Introdução: O pé diabético é uma das complicações do diabetes mellitus e pode ocasionar úlceras de difícil cicatrização, infecções e amputações de membros inferiores. Nesse contexto, a laserterapia tem sido investigada como recurso complementar para favorecer a reparação tecidual e contribuir para o tratamento dessas lesões. Objetivo: avaliar a utilização da laserterapia como recurso fisioterapêutico no tratamento de pacientes com úlceras do pé diabético.  Materiais e Método: Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, realizada a partir da análise de 15 estudos científicos publicados entre 2022 e 2026, incluindo ensaios clínicos, estudos de caso, revisão bibliográfica, estudo observacional e pesquisas exploratórias. Os trabalhos selecionados abordaram diferentes modalidades de laserterapia aplicadas ao tratamento de úlceras do pé diabético. Resultados e discussão: Os estudos analisados apontam resultados promissores quanto ao uso da laserterapia como recurso complementar no tratamento de úlceras do pé diabético, com potencial para favorecer a cicatrização e a recuperação dos tecidos. Contribuição Científica: O estudo contribui para ampliar o conhecimento sobre a aplicação da laserterapia no tratamento do pé diabético, destacando suas possibilidades terapêuticas e a importância de sua associação aos cuidados convencionais e às medidas de autocuidado. Conclusão: A laserterapia pode auxiliar na cicatrização das úlceras do pé diabético, como complemento ao tratamento convencional, sendo a Fisioterapia importante em sua aplicação e acompanhamento.</jats:p>

                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-5">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>To examine whether there are associations between the neighborhood exposome at birth and EAA trajectories from early childhood through adolescence.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-6">
                    <jats:title>Design, Setting, and Participants</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This longitudinal cohort study used data from Project Viva, a prebirth cohort that enrolled pregnant women in eastern Massachusetts from April 22, 1999, to July 31, 2002. Participants included 570 children with available peripheral blood DNA methylation data, complete neighborhood characteristics, and complete covariates. Data were analyzed from August 19, 2024, to August 21, 2026.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-7">
                    <jats:title>Exposures</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Neighborhood exposome profiles at birth derived from 22 census tract–level characteristics across 4 domains (area deprivation, social fragmentation, population density, and environmental quality) using self-organizing maps.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-8">
                    <jats:title>Main Outcomes and Measures</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>EAA was calculated at 3, 8, and 13 years of age using the Horvath, Skin &amp;amp; Blood, and Wu epigenetic clocks. Trajectories were identified using latent class linear mixed models. Associations between neighborhood profiles and EAA trajectories were estimated using multinomial mixed models.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-9">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Among 570 children (mean [SD] age at early childhood, 3.2 [0.4] years; 305 [53.5%] male), 3 EAA trajectory groups (stable, increasing, and decreasing for the Horvath and Skin &amp;amp; Blood clocks or low-baseline for the Wu clock) and 3 neighborhood profiles were identified. Compared with profile 1 (suburban, lowest adverse exposures [n = 278]), children born into profile 2 (urban, high residential instability and single-person households, and highway proximity [n = 168]) had greater odds of increasing EAA for the Wu clock (adjusted odds ratio, 1.67 [95% CI, 1.03-2.69]). Profile 3 (urban, high socioeconomic deprivation and pollution [n = 124]) showed no associations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="ab-zoi261190-10">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions and Relevance</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In this longitudinal cohort study, birth into neighborhoods characterized by high residential instability and single-person households and highway proximity was associated with increasing Wu EAA trajectories across childhood. These findings suggest that early-life neighborhood conditions, encompassing both social and physical environmental factors, may represent targets for interventions aimed at reducing long-term disease risk. Further research is needed to clarify the implications of these findings for later health and prevention.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The exploration of topological states has emerged as a vibrant frontier across diverse physical systems. Among these, the Möbius strip stands out as a canonical structure that has recently inspired intriguing optical physics. In this work, we extend this concept into the high‐dimensional realm by using an optical analogue—the optical Möbius snail. Specifically, employing a skyrmionic beam as the input field, tight focusing yields a continuous family of Möbius strips that exist in three‐dimensional space, giving rise to a snail‐like polarization topological texture. Furthermore, we demonstrate full‐field polarization tomography and achieve switchable control of this optical snail texture by tuning the Skyrme number of the incident skyrmionic beam. Our findings establish a direct bridge between low‐ and high‐dimensional Möbius geometries, opening a new platform for exploring complex spatial topology and tailored light‐matter interactions.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Geometric phases have long been confined to the cross‐polarized channel under circularly polarized incidence. Their manipulation in the co‐polarized channel remains challenging. Exceptional points (EPs), where eigenvalues and eigenvectors simultaneously coalesce in non‐Hermitian systems, provide topological degrees of freedom for field manipulation. Using temporal coupled‐mode theory (TCMT), we demonstrate EPs in the co‐polarized transmission channel of broadband high‐transmission metasurfaces. The metasurfaces comprise a multilayer metal‐dielectric structure with top and bottom patches connected by metallized vias. Counter‐rotation of the metallic layers breaks out‐of‐plane mirror symmetry and introduces structural chirality. This produces direction‐asymmetric effective coupling in a selected circular‐polarization channel while the full electromagnetic system remains Lorentz reciprocal. By tailoring the projected input and output coupling parameters, the scattering operator is brought to Jordan form, thereby constructing EPs in the co‐polarized channel. The EPs introduce phase singularities and branch cuts that reconstruct the winding behavior and phase evolution of the complex transmission trajectory in parameter space, thereby reshaping the conventional geometric‐phase accumulation. Using the reconstructed phase response, we realize broadband, high‐efficiency, large‐angle wavefront decoupling of orthogonal circularly polarized channels. This work extends EP‐based topological phase manipulation to the co‐polarized channel and provides a platform for broadband, direction‐asymmetric, polarization‐stable transmissive wavefront shaping.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Laser-based visible-light communication (VLC) can exploit wavelength and polarization multiplexing, but amplifier, channel, and coherent-receiver impairments interact. This paper develops an impairment-aware simulation of an eight-wavelength, dual-circular-polarization link carrying a 380.16-MHz occupied orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) resource grid within a nominal 400-MHz fifth-generation New Radio (5G NR)-aligned channel. The model includes laser-diode/semiconductor-optical-amplifier (LD–SOA) saturation and amplified spontaneous emission, wavelength-dependent gain ripple, Lambertian line-of-sight loss, residual wavelength-division-multiplexing (WDM) crosstalk, polarization mixing, coherent-receiver noise, phase/frequency offsets, and quadrature imbalance. The receiver combines covariance whitening, pilot-estimated 2 × 2 regularized multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) separation, pilot-assisted phase correction, and damped decision-directed refinement. With quadrature phase-shift keying, the nominal net payload rate after applying a 7 % FEC-overhead factor for rate reporting is 8.527 Gb/s. In the controlled reference realization, the proposed receiver remains below the 3.8 × 10
                    <jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>
                    pre-FEC bit-error-rate screening level through 50 m. A receiver ablation shows that both Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization and symmetric covariance whitening remove most of the reference I/Q-imbalance penalty, while the decision-directed update provides a smaller incremental improvement near the reach boundary. A separate sweep gives 17.054 Gb/s with 16-level quadrature-amplitude modulation through 16 m. The results provide a traceable baseline for joint optical-front-end and coherent-receiver design.
                  </jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Based on the energy confinement time scaling law of stellarator in the low-confinement mode, combined with energy balance equation and the plasma propagation and power deposition equations of the electron cyclotron wave in the three-dimensional magnetic field, a stellarator plasma start-up model including electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) and impurity radiation power loss is established. Validation against W7-X experimental data demonstrates good agreement in the temporal evolution of electron temperature and radiation losses, which verified that the model can correctly give the plasma start-up results of the stellarator under ECRH. This model is applied to predict the results of plasma start-up under 28 GHz ECRH for China Helical Device 1 (CN-H1) stellarator. The effects of the initial electron-to-ion temperature ratio (Te/Ti), ECRH injection power (Pinj), deposition position and effective charge number Z_{\text{eff}} on start-up are systematically studied and analyzed. The results show that the initial Te/Ti ratio affects only the ramp-up rate, while the final steady-state electron and ion temperature remain unaffected. Higher Pinj accelerates electron temperature rise and increases flat-top electron temperature, whereas the ion temperature exhibits the opposite trend, decreasing with increasing Pinj. The deposition location has a decisive impact on the start-up outcome: only core deposition on the low-field side leads to a successful start-up, while high-field side and off-axis low-field side depositions fail owing to refractive deviation of the ray trajectory and insufficient absorption, respectively. The steady-state electron and ion temperatures are insensitive to {\mathrm{Z}}_{\text{eff}} within a reasonable range.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Brain metastases (BM) are the most common intracranial malignancy in adults and remain associated with poor morbididty and mortality despite advances in multimodal therapy. Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) offers a minimally invasive approach to assess disease biology, but its relationship to clinical, radiographic, and survival outcomes in BM remains poorly characterized.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We retrospectively analyzed perioperative plasma cfDNA concentration in 108 consecutive patients who underwent surgical resection of BM from breast cancer, lung cancer, or melanoma between 2010 and 2019. cfDNA was extracted from peripheral plasma and quantified by fluorometric assay. Patients were dichotomized at cfDNA &gt;21 ng/mL, corresponding to the upper tertile.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Plasma cfDNA was elevated in patients with uncontrolled systemic disease (p = 0.013) and leptomeningeal disease (p = 0.002), but was not associated with intracranial tumor volume, lesion number, edema volume, or proximity to CSF or venous structures. High cfDNA was associated with worse OS across the full cohort (p = 0.044), but not PFS or cumulative incidence of intracranial progression. This OS association was most pronounced in melanoma BM (p &lt; 0.001), with no significant association in breast or lung BM. On univariate Cox regression, cfDNA concentration was associated with worse OS (HR 1.01/ng/mL, 95% CI 1.00–1.01, p = 0.048), along with uncontrolled systemic disease, high BM volume, lower KPS, partial resection, and prior hormonal/immunotherapy.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Perioperative plasma cfDNA concentration tracks systemic disease burden rather than intracranial tumor load and carries prognostic significance for overall survival in patients with BM. The histology-dependent nature of this association, particularly in melanoma, warrants validation in larger, molecularly annotated cohorts. These findings highlight the need for more sensitive, CNS-directed liquid biopsy strategies to capture intracranial disease burden.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract:
<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Cold atmospheric plasma is applied to dental implants for surface activation, osseointegration, infection control and host modulation. This review reads those four uses as one reactive‐species mechanism with a separate exposure axis per target (an organizing interpretation, not a measured law) and audits what an illustrative sample of thirty‐three protocols reports about dose. Plasma medicine has a source‐characterization specification (DIN SPEC 91315) and candidate dose descriptors, delivered energy and equivalent total oxidation potential, whose inputs no audited protocol reports in full. Of twenty‐five atmospheric‐pressure protocols, working gas is stated in twenty‐four, flow in nineteen, power or voltage setting in eleven; across all thirty‐three, treated area and delivered dose in none, a measured output in two. Human endpoints are mostly surrogates.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>We start with a brief introduction to the many faces of the Sun, the dynamic star that is the main source of space weather. We explain the need for spacecraft observations, the structure of the solar atmosphere, and the Sun’s magnetic cycle. Next, we focus on the Sun’s influence on Earth, define ‘space weather,’ and briefly discuss its effects on our technology and related socio-economic impacts. Then, we present data-driven, physics-based simulation models with predictive capabilities that enable forecasting and mitigation. We focus on models developed by my team at KU Leuven and the results and predictions they produce: the heliospheric wind and CME evolution models EUHFORIA and ICARUS, the global solar corona model COCONUT, and the solar energetic particle acceleration and transport model Particle Radiation Asset Directed at IP Space Exploration. We end with a few take-home messages.</jats:p>

title: Maternal plasma cell-free RNAs and sonographic parameters for predicting spontaneous preterm birth in twin pregnancies: A prospective cohort study
abstract:
<jats:p>Objective: To evaluate whether cervical length (CL), uterocervical angle (UCA), and five maternal plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNAs) markers can predict spontaneous preterm birth (sPTB) before 37 and 34 weeks in twin pregnancies.
Methods: This prospective study included 80 twin pregnancies examined at 14 - 24 weeks’ gestation at Hai Phong Medical University Hospital, from February 2023 to February 2025. CL and UCA were measured by transvaginal ultrasonography, and plasma cfRNA concentrations of PSME2, NAMPT, APOA1, APOA4, and Hsa-let-7g were quantified using droplet digital PCR. Participants were followed until delivery. Associations with sPTB were assessed using multivariable binary logistic regression, and predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis.
Results: Women who delivered preterm had a significantly larger UCA and shorter CL than those delivering at term. Among the five RNA markers, only Hsa-let-7g differed significantly between women with sPTB before 34 weeks and those delivering at or after 34 weeks (1.89 ± 0.51 vs. 1.03 ± 0.54, p = 0.024). After adjusting, UCA was independently associated with sPTB before 37 weeks (OR 1.042, 95% CI 1.005 - 1.081) and before 34 weeks (OR 1.056, 95% CI 1.004 - 1.111). Hsa-let-7g was associated with sPTB before 34 weeks (OR 3.391, 95% CI 1.089 - 10.556). Area under the curve for predicting sPTB before 34 weeks was 0.799 for UCA, 0.712 for Hsa-let-7g, and 0.829 for their combination.
Conclusion: Second-trimester UCA and plasma Hsa-let-7g showed potential as non-invasive markers for predicting sPTB in twin pregnancies. Their combined use may improve the prediction of sPTB before 34 weeks.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Plasma liquid biopsy offers a minimally invasive strategy for glioblastoma (GBM) monitoring, but assay sensitivity remains limited. We evaluated a matched tumor-plasma whole exome sequencing (WES) approach to longitudinally detect somatic variants in plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) during chemoradiotherapy (CRT).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Plasma cfDNA was collected from 8 patients with GBM at baseline, intra-CRT, and after CRT (NCT05480644). Tumor tissue and plasma WES were performed by Caris Life Sciences. Variants were called and filtered using the Genome Analysis Toolkit. Timepoint-matched genomic DNA (gDNA; from buffy coat) served as matched normal for serial cfDNA analyses; baseline gDNA served as the matched normal for tumor analyses. Coding variants were defined as protein-altering/splice-site variants, including missense, truncating, frameshift, in-frame indel, start/stop codon, and splice-site alterations. dbSNP-annotated variants were removed.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Median patient age was 58 years (interquartile range [IQR] 36-66); 62% were male. All patients received conventionally fractionated radiotherapy (59.4Gy/33fx) with concurrent temozolomide. Tumor and plasma WES generated 9,213 and 16,032 variant calls, respectively. Variants absent from matched normal gDNA (cfDNA-only) were detectable with median VAF of 6.4% (range 0.104-95.9%) and 9.1% (range 0.316-68.4%) in tumor and plasma samples, respectively. Across patients, 128 unique cfDNA-only variants were present in matched tumor and plasma, including 21 coding variants. Tumor-concordant cfDNA-only variant counts were highest at baseline and decreased during/after RT. This decrease was significant by paired Wilcoxon testing (p &lt; 0.02) and was not associated with differences in median variant read depth. A subset of tumor-concordant variants (n = 21) persisted across serial plasma timepoints.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This exploratory pilot study demonstrates longitudinal tumor-informed plasma WES is feasible during CRT for GBM and may identify dynamic tumor-concordant cfDNA variants. Plasma variants were not dominated by canonical GBM driver alterations, suggesting that longitudinal, tumor-informed plasma cfDNA WES may capture broader low-frequency molecular patterns beyond isolated detection of established tumor-defining events.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

abstract: <jats:p>O envelhecimento cutâneo é um processo biológico multifatorial caracterizado pela degradação da integridade estrutural e da matriz extracelular (MEC). Para mitigar essas alterações morfológicas, a medicina regenerativa tem impulsionado terapias minimamente invasivas baseadas em hemoderivados. Este estudo tem como objetivo avaliar e comparar a eficácia clínica, a segurança e os mecanismos de ação tecidual das terapias autólogas de primeira e segunda geração, destacando a indispensabilidade da atuação técnica do biomédico na padronização pré-analítica. Trata-se de uma Revisão Integrativa da Literatura conduzida nas bases de dados PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science e BVS/LILACS. Após o rigoroso delineamento de elegibilidade, 15 artigos científicos (publicados entre 2020 e 2026) compuseram a amostra final. Os achados demonstram que, enquanto os concentrados de primeira geração apresentam uma liberação rápida de fatores de crescimento (bolus), a segunda geração forma uma rede tridimensional fisiológica, garantindo uma eluição sustentada e o aprisionamento funcional de leucócitos. Clinicamente, ambas as terapias induzem expressiva neocolagenogênese e aumento da espessura dérmica. Topograficamente, a segunda geração demonstra superioridade no preenchimento estrutural periorbital (textura e crepitação), enquanto a primeira se destaca no clareamento de hiperpigmentações infraorbitais. A acentuada heterogeneidade nos protocolos de centrifugação figura como o principal gargalo metodológico da literatura atual. Conclui-se que essas matrizes constituem estratégias altamente eficazes, contudo, o domínio sobre a fisiologia do processamento e a padronização operacional (força g e tempo) pelo biomédico são determinantes para a reprodutibilidade clínica e a segurança do paciente.</jats:p>

title: A simple model for evaporation-driven migration of liquid metal between plasma pulses in a fusion reactor with liquid metal plasma-facing components

affiliation.name: Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Liquid metal plasma-facing components (PFCs) are being considered for a variety of fusion power plant designs, and careful control of the liquid metal inventory will be essential in these systems to mitigate challenges with liquid metal corrosion and hydrogen fuel retention. Since many power plant designs and existing test facilities rely on pulsed plasma sources, it is critical to understand how liquid metal evaporation leads to material migration within a reactor over the periods of time when no plasma is present. This work addresses this question by developing a simple particle balance model to efficiently calculate liquid metal vapor transport patterns over indefinitely long time periods, using a particle redistribution matrix to capture the vapor transport details. After developing the mathematical model, characteristics of a future Liquid Metal Core-Edge (LMCE) research facility with liquid lithium divertors are used as a reference to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used. Examples of lithium migration during the cooldown period between plasma pulses show that the pattern of lithium deposition depends primarily on the system geometry. An important secondary effect in these scenarios is the relative cooldown rate of the lithium divertor with respect to other PFCs in the device. Examples are also provided to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used to optimize the design of a cold finger to collect liquid metal condensation for extraction and reprocessing, with the results showing that a future LMCE facility may be capable of collecting all of the lithium evaporated between plasma pulses if the main chamber walls can be maintained above 350 C during operation.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Physics‐based ground‐motion (GM) simulations are being increasingly adopted in engineering practice. Nonetheless, computational requirements remain a hindrance to explicitly considering the exhaustive number of potential ruptures in typical probabilistic seismic hazard analysis (PSHA) calculations. We present a framework for simulation‐consistent PSHA that combines direct simulation of the ruptures contributing most strongly to the hazard with a surrogate model, trained on physics‐based ground‐motion simulations, to represent the much larger number of ruptures that have individually small, but collectively meaningful, contributions. We illustrate the approach through application to the CyberShake NZ dataset, which collectively includes explicit simulation of approximately 16,000 rupture realisations across New Zealand (NZ) for the fault‐based component of the hazard, while a surrogate model is used to quantify the contributions from the distributed seismicity component of the hazard. The surrogate model is based on a neural network that includes common predictor variables present in contemporary ergodic empirical ground‐motion models, as well as the addition of location dependence. The large number of simulations available for training simulation‐based surrogate models avoids issues with prior attempts to develop machine learning‐based ground motion models with only observational data, and the straightforward model training process means that surrogate models can be iteratively re‐trained as simulation methods and their constituent models and input data continue to evolve. A principal benefit of the use of simulation‐based surrogate models is achieving a unified simulation‐based treatment of the ground‐motion model component in PSHA (within typical computational constraints), in contrast to prior studies that have used simulations for the fault‐based sources but conventional empirical models for distributed seismicity sources.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Brain metastases (BMs) remain a critical challenge in oncology with limited tools for real-time molecular monitoring. Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) has transformed treatment monitoring in extracranial cancers, but whether cfDNA can reliably detect and track intracranial disease remains unclear. We performed serial cfDNA sequencing in a cohort of patients with BMs of diverse histologies treated with pembrolizumab on a phase 2 trial (Brastianos et al., Nat Med 2023). Ultra-low-pass whole genome sequencing (ULP-WGS) was performed on serial plasma samples and CSF (where available) with tumor fraction (TF) estimated by ichorCNA (limit of detection ∼3%). Targeted sequencing was performed on matched tissue (BM, primaries, extracranial metastases) and plasma to assess tissue-plasma mutation concordance. Advanced quantitative MRI including DCE permeability (ktrans) and DSC perfusion was obtained at serial timepoints. 238 serial plasma ULP-WGS samples were collected from 57 patients (median 4 per patient). Among 36 patients with pre-treatment samples, 20 had baseline plasma TF below the limit of detection. Detectable baseline TF trended toward shorter overall survival (5.2 vs 8.3 months, p = 0.06). In 17 patients with matched tissue and plasma targeted sequencing, overall tissue-to-plasma mutation concordance was 65% but varied dramatically by patient (11-100%). Concordance strongly correlated with baseline plasma TF (rho=0.87, p = 0.005) and was similar across tissue compartments (BM 62%, extracranial metastasis 66%, primary 55%). MRI-derived BBB permeability (ktrans) did not correlate with plasma TF (rho=-0.02, p = 0.96; n = 18), indicating shedding constraints extend beyond vascular permeability. All CSF samples analyzed (n = 4) had readily detectable TF (range 4.4-45.7%). Plasma cfDNA has limited sensitivity for detecting and monitoring BM, with most patients below reliable detection thresholds. This limitation is not explained by BBB vascular permeability alone, suggesting alternative biological mechanisms restrict tumor DNA shedding from intracranial disease. CSF-based and ultra-sensitive sequencing approaches warrant investigation for molecular monitoring in this population.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>
                    Treatment for plasma cell dyscrasias imposes burdens on patients and caregivers, particularly for cellular therapies. Traditional social determinants of health may not capture caregiver availability. We conducted a cross‐sectional survey through HealthTree. Patients categorized their caregiver support through a single question: cohabiting dedicated caregiver, non‐cohabiting dedicated caregiver, arrangeable support when needed or inadequate support. Among 1231 respondents, 68% had live‐in caregivers, 3% had dedicated non‐cohabiting caregivers, 23% arranged support when needed and 5% struggled to find support. Living arrangement had the strongest correlation with caregiver availability: 85% of married patients had live‐in support compared to 6%–12% among divorced, widowed or never‐married patients. Live‐in caregiver support was lower in females than males (63% vs. 76%, respectively,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     < 0.001), and in Black versus White patients (46% vs. 71%, respectively,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     = 0.002). Employment, education level, distance from treatment centres and insurance type showed no association. Caregiver support for patients with plasma cell dyscrasias is primarily determined by household structure. Despite selection bias in our cohort, one‐third of patients lacked dedicated caregiving assistance and 5% actively struggled to secure help. No single demographic variable reliably predicts caregiver availability, emphasizing the need for direct assessment as a standard question in clinical and research settings.
                  </jats:p>

                    <jats:sc>bstract</jats:sc>

                  <jats:p>Collisions of ultra-relativistic bubbles during cosmological phase transitions can produce particles much heavier than the transition scale. Previous analyses modelled this process as the off-shell decay of the scalar background. We show that its results parametrically overestimate hard particle production and depend on the gauge choice and the coordinate choice in field space. We propose an alternative formalism, analogous to the partonic description of high-energy collisions. In the ultra-relativistic limit, the colliding bubbles undergo nearly free passage and hard production arises from on-shell scatterings among the quanta constituting the Lorentz-contracted walls. We apply this approach to heavy scalar, fermion, and vector particle production, and study the implications for dark matter, leptogenesis, graviton production and primordial gravitational waves.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Plasma membrane integrity is essential for cellular survival, yet how cells repair micron-scale plasma membrane ruptures remains poorly understood. Here, using the genetically tractable Caenorhabditis elegans epidermis, we combine live imaging, genetics, super-resolution microscopy, and biophysical approaches to define a size-dependent role for endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRT)-III in large-scale membrane repair. Small wounds induce transient, focal VPS-32 accumulation, whereas large wounds trigger the formation of a persistent but dynamic, circumferential ESCRT-III assembly that remains associated with the wound during repair. Formation of this assembly requires conserved ESCRT regulators, including ALX-1, TSG-101, and VPS-4, together with VPS-32 polymerization. The wound-associated ESCRT-III assembly is required for membrane tension restoration and efficient membrane repair, while disrupting VPS-32 polymerization impairs tension recovery, reduces vesicle recruitment and wound closure, and consequently compromises axon regeneration and organismal survival following injury. Together, our findings suggest that large plasma membrane wounds induce a persistent, dynamic ESCRT-III assembly that restores membrane tension and facilitates vesicle-mediated membrane addition to promote wound repair.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Power distribution networks are a critical component of the electric power distribution system. Hence, numerous research has focus on distribution network reconfiguration systems, intending to minimize power losses and interruptions, namely, Customer Average Interruption Index (CAIDI), System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI), Energy Not Supplied (ENS), and Voltage Profile (VP) improvement, either by Genetic Algorithm (GA) or Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Nonetheless, existing research has not simultaneously employed a hybrid of GA and PSO optimization methods to ascertain which optimization method is better in terms of improving the reliability indices, such as CAIDI, SAIFI, and ENS, while minimizing power losses and improving the VP, thus leaving a gap in the literature. Hence, the proposed research work seeks to utilize the synergy of GA and PSO optimization techniques on the IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 69-bus systems with the aforementioned reliability targets to unearth which of the optimization techniques is better than the other. Meanwhile, the obtained results indicate that the GA exhibits a higher voltage level enhancement of 2.75% with a corresponding SAIFI reduction of 33%. Nonetheless, the PSO unveils superior or enhanced power loss reduction of 61.75%, ENS reduction of 48%, and CAIDI reduction of 30% with a corresponding computational speed of 0.24 seconds. Hence, based on the aforementioned analysis of the results, it can be concluded that the selection of the optimization algorithm depends on the network's specific operational requirements, as no single algorithm performs optimally across all parameter measurements. Besides, while the PSO performs excellently in terms of loss, ENS, and CAIDI reduction, the GA performs well in terms of voltage enhancement and SAIDI reduction.</jats:p>

abstract: <jats:p>Presentation of antigen from necrotic cancer cells within tumour microenvironments to T cells requires efficient uptake by DCs. However, intact necrotic tumour cells present physical barriers to direct endocytosis. Here, we investigate the non-canonical role of the serine protease plasmin and its regulatory network in tumour cell endocytosis by human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (mDCs) and downstream T cell stimulation. Pre-treating heat-killed melanoma cells with plasmin significantly enhanced their endocytosis by mDCs, an effect reversed by the physiological inhibitor α2-antiplasmin. Live-cell imaging and flow cytometry demonstrated that mDCs predominantly internalise micron-scale cellular debris rather than whole cells, and that plasmin activity “digests” dead-cell particles, thereby enabling uptake of particles of optimal diameter (∼1-3 μm). Enhanced endocytosis directly translated to increased CD4+ T cell activation. Furthermore, both heat-killed melanoma cells and mDCs functioned as lysine-dependent plasminogen-binding surfaces capable of generating localised proteolytic activity. Plasmin treatment modestly reduced DC cell-surface PD-L1 expression and altered specific inflammatory cytokines. These findings reframe plasmin as a modulator of immune-tumour interactions and highlight important methodological considerations regarding serum-derived proteases in experimental immunology.</jats:p>

abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Urethral stricture is a common and debilitating urological condition in which fibrosis narrows the urethral lumen. Recurrence after surgical repair is frequent, and no antifibrotic pharmacotherapy has been established. Extracellular vesicles from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUC-MSC-EVs) show antifibrotic activity in several organ systems, but whether they act in urethral fibrosis, and by what mechanism, had not been examined.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We isolated and characterized hUC-MSC-EVs and tested them in primary human urethral fibroblasts (UFBs) stimulated with TGF-β1 and in a rat model of trauma-induced urethral stricture. Small RNA sequencing was used to profile the EV miRNA cargo, and the role of let-7i-5p was examined by gain- and loss-of-function experiments, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and let-7i-5p-depleted EVs (KD EVs), both
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      and
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      .
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      hUC-MSC-EVs dose-dependently suppressed TGF-β1-induced UFB proliferation, migration and myofibroblast differentiation and lowered α-SMA and Collagen I expression, with reduced Smad2/3 phosphorylation. Periurethral injection in rats significantly reduced urethral wall hyperechogenicity, luminal narrowing, submucosal collagen deposition and profibrotic protein expression at the 4-week postoperative endpoint. Small RNA sequencing placed let-7i-5p among the most abundant miRNAs packaged in hUC-MSC-EVs, and this miRNA was efficiently transferred to recipient UFBs. let-7i-5p bound the 3′-UTR of TGFBR1 and suppressed TGFBR1 expression at both mRNA and protein levels. Depleting let-7i-5p from EVs with an inhibitor largely abolished their antifibrotic activity
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      and
                      <jats:italic>in vitro</jats:italic>
                      , linking EV-delivered let-7i-5p to suppression of the TGFBR1/Smad2/3 signaling axis.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These results identify hUC-MSC-EVs as an injectable, cell-free antifibrotic candidate for urethral stricture and let-7i-5p as a cargo on which their activity depends.</jats:p>
